Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 63, English)
Time, Destiny , and the Science of Jal Tatva: How Chakras, Infection, and Kundalini Actually Work

Sour ce: A live, highly interactive satsang/hawan session with extensive sangat participation (multiple named and unnamed members asking rapid-fir e questions, including r eferences to "Ankur Bhaiya," "Anshu," and "Harshvar dhan"). This document is Part I of III — Knowledge Base, Q&A Pairs, and Curated Conversational Q&A.

1. Opening teaching: time is powerful even over God. Per this teaching, illustrated through the Ramayana — Bhagwan Ram knew Sita Mata was with Ravana, yet still waited through an entire monsoon month (Sawan) before acting, telling no one. Even Sugriv , Ram's close friend, for got his promise to help during this period under the influence of "maya." When Lakshman questioned this, Ram explained that Sugriv had not truly for gotten — the spell of maya during this waiting period deliberately obscures things, and nothing can be done to counter it until the appointed time arrives.

2. Even Hanuman Ji Maharaj was subject to this same principle. Per this teaching, despite being described as "gyani gunam agraganyam" (foremost among the wise) and constantly absorbed in Ram-chintan, Hanuman Ji Maharaj himself remained unaware of the need to help Sugriv for the entire Sawan month — illustrating that "samay bada balwan" (time is exceedingly powerful) applies even to the greatest devotees.

3. The Ankur Bhaiya example — a modern parallel. Per this teaching, a devotee ("Ankur Bhaiya") was not permitted to visit/join for two months; the moment permission was granted and he bowed at Gurudev's feet, he was instantly "awakened" (jagrit) — illustrating that timing is entirely in the guru's hands, not the devotee's.

4. Fate/destiny cannot be br oken except thr ough the guru's will. Per this teaching, anyone who believes they can personally "break" or forcibly alter their own destiny is mistaken — such a change is possible only if and when the practitioner's guru wills it.

5. Guidance for handling adverse periods. Per this teaching, when facing an unfavorable/adverse period, a person should focus purely on self-protection ("bachav") rather than playing on the "front foot" (taking aggressive or risky action) — the recommended approach is to seek the guru's help and guidance during such times.

6. Warning against ego/pride when things go well thr ough one's own practice. Per this teaching, sitting in a position of spiritual capability can sometimes create the illusion that one's own words/actions alone are responsible for results — Bhaiya notes that his Gurudev repeatedly reminds practitioners that they remain human, precisely to keep this ego in check, since this pattern of adverse periods and tests happens to everyone in life, even to God himself (as illustrated by the Ram story above).

7. Recommended starting point for new members. Per this teaching, first-time attendees should watch the "Mool Tatva" (Fundamental Element) video and begin their own jaap alongside it, aiming for a minimum count of 15–20 lakh (1.5–2 million) repetitions — described as an achievable tar get, after which Ashaeiynn can begin sending focused shaktis to that practitioner for a genuinely beneficial ef fect.

8. The long-term effect of 3+ years of drishti/practice. Per this teaching, someone with roughly three years of sustained practice develops an accompanying unseen power ("adrishya shakti") that supports them at every step — advising on right and wrong, showing the path forward, and revealing "the other world" alongside this one. Two specific benefits are named: access to one's own personal guru-guidance, and one's own mantra shakti, which can elevate consciousness to an extreme level and develop genuine manifestation power — whatever the person genuinely wishes for is described as eventually and certainly occurring, though not necessarily immediately ("aaj nahi kal").

9. Manifestation and one's own planetary influences (grahas). Per this teaching, if a desired outcome does not conflict with a person's own grahas (astrological influences), it can occur quickly; if it does conflict, it will be delayed until that graha's influencing period naturally passes — but it is still described as certain to eventually occur . If a person's mantra shakti is strong enough to actively resolve/settle the graha's obstruction with directed ener gy , the outcome can occur much faster .

10. Warning about desiring things outside one's own destiny/grahas. Per this teaching, if someone forcefully manifests something that was never meant to be theirs (not within their own grahas/destiny), "the whole universe" turns against them — because whatever was taken was, in ef fect, taken from whoever it was actually destined for , and that displaced ef fect inevitably seeks some form of retribution. Practitioners are advised to keep their own ener gy reserves strong ("stall") specifically to be able to absorb and rebound from this kind of backlash.

1 1. Drishti (subtle sight) is framed as a "necessary evil." Per this teaching, it is "necessary" because without it a person remains confused/misled (bhramit), forced to wander between dif ferent babas, pandits, and pirs/fakirs seeking answers; it is "evil" in the sense that it makes a person far more consciously alert/active than before, requiring vigilance over even small details — described as a responsibility with both a good and a dif ficult side, which is not entirely within the practitioner's own choice to accept or decline once a certain point is reached.

12. A genuine third-eye aspirant does not cr edit themselves for outcomes. Per this teaching, someone with two-plus years of experience within Ashaeiynn will never claim "it happened because of me" — they instead recognize that whatever happens is what "Ram rach rakha" (what Ram has already ordained), while still continuing to make sincere ef fort, because such practitioners begin perceiving realities that are otherwise imperceptible.

13. Intr oduction to this session's cor e teaching: the science of "Jal Tatva" (water element) and infection. Per this teaching, this is a vidya (knowledge/practice) specifically related to the water element, composed of what Bhaiya calls 1 1 anu (particles) and 21 mahanu (gr eat-particles) — described as the underlying subtle science behind what is today commonly called "infection."

14. What "infection" is, described in familiar biological terms first. Per this teaching, infection is framed conventionally as any foreign/alien particle entering the body , which the body's immune system (white blood cells) resists, producing inflammation, and it is this inflammation that manifests as infection.

15. The "Dwait Sangam" — a subtle confluence between 1 1 anu and 21 mahanu. Per this teaching, there exists a significant confluence point ("dwait sangam") between the 1 1 anu and 21 mahanu, connected to four lokas — not the conventional earth/sky/netherworld triad, but four distinct horizontal and vertical layers/columns existing in the space between the earth's surface and the sky , centered in between.

16. All chakras ar e fundamentally made of Jal Tatva (water element) — not of separate distinct elements. Per this teaching, contrary to common belief that dif ferent chakras correspond to dif ferent elements (fire, water , air, earth, etc. with dif ferent colors), the actual underlying substance of every chakra is water; only their outward colors dif fer, while the underlying ener gy is fundamentally uniform, being water -based.

17. How chakras actually form and function, mechanically . Per this teaching, chakras exist as tiny droplet-like clusters of water - element molecules (compared to the dif ference between ordinary H2O and highly condensed/distilled "H3O"-like dense water) which arrange themselves into distinct structures at each chakra location; when ener gy strikes these water -molecule clusters, they rotate and emit their characteristic color as a "beam."

18. Why the body is r oughly 70% water , and why this matters for chakras. Per this teaching, since the body's chakras are fundamentally water -based, this directly explains the commonly cited fact that approximately 70% of the human body is water — and explains folk warnings like "one drop of contaminated water can ruin everything," since jal tatva underlies the entire chakra system.

19. Fir e (agni) does not consume jal tatva — it transforms/r elocates it. Per this teaching, when agni (fire) increases in the body , the jal tatva does not disappear or decrease — it transforms (evaporates, like steam) and physically migrates from a lower position to a higher one, retaining its water -based nature throughout, rather than being consumed or lost.

20. Chakras can shift position (displacement) — a cor e, non-obvious teaching. Per this teaching, chakras do not remain permanently fixed in one place ("apna sthaan ya roop nahi chodte" is presented as a common misconception) — in reality , a chakra can leave its usual location and "circulate," reforming at a new position once the rising water -element ener gy (carried upward by fire) reaches a place with a suitable "climate"/condition, condensing there and taking on a chakra-form again.

21. What "sahasrar tak kundalini shakti pahunch gayi" (kundalini energy has r eached the cr own chakra) actually means, mechanically . Per this teaching, this specific claim means that the practitioner's jal-tatva-based chakra ener gy — normally located at a lower position — has, through suf ficiently intense agni, been carried and relocated all the way up to the crown (sahasrar) position; it is described in this teaching as displacement of jal tatva via agni, shaped en route by vayu (air).

22. Why external "power -ups" (shaktipat/kundalini awakening fr om someone else) can sometimes leave a person mor e vulnerable to negativity . Per this teaching, when someone else's power is used to forcibly push a practitioner's own chakra ener gy far higher than the practitioner's own agni (personal fire/tapasya capacity) can naturally sustain or "reach," a gap forms between where the ener gy now sits and where the practitioner's own fire can actually operate — leaving the practitioner ef fectively unable to draw on their prayer/mantra shakti at that new , elevated position, and thus more exposed to negativity , even though standard aura checks may show "nothing wrong" (because nothing negative is literally seated in the old, now-vacated position).

23. "Positive push" — when a saint's blessing genuinely does work. Per this teaching, when a saint or great soul (mahrishi) of fers a genuine "positive push," they lift a practitioner's chakra ener gy to a far higher Dimension (the example given is up to the 100th Dimension) and ef fectively "reserve" that higher -Dimension shakti for the practitioner in advance — but this reserved shakti only becomes actually accessible once the practitioner ignites their own personal agni (fire/tapasya) strongly enough to reach and draw on it; without that personal ef fort, the blessing remains present but inert.

24. Why some genuine saints get unfairly accused of being "frauds" ("dhongi"). Per this teaching, when the practitioner's own agni never becomes strong enough to reach the elevated Dimension a saint's blessing has reserved for them, the promised results simply never materialize for that person — leading outside observers to wrongly conclude the saint's blessing itself was fake, when in reality the saint (and the deity-power acting through them) did nothing wrong; the shortfall is in the recipient's own undeveloped agni, not in the blessing's authenticity .

25. The three primary ways to incr ease one's own agni (fir e/inner energy), per this teaching. (1) Mantra jaap, which steadily raises agni; (2) Tapasya/vrat (austerity/fasting) — described as "reducing external intake," letting internal tap (inner heat/discipline) build up on its own; and (3) Havan, described as the single fastest and most powerful method for rapidly increasing agni tatva.

26. Lord Shiva's own teaching on tapasya vs. mantra jaap, r eferenced here. Per this teaching, per Lord Shiva's own stated wisdom, the fruit ("phal") of a thousand havans exists within a single mantra jaap performed by a true tapasvi (one practicing sustained tapasya and unbroken brahmacharya) — but this specific equivalence requires genuinely sustained, unbroken tapasya and brahmacharya; absent that level of personal discipline, havan remains the most accessible, reliable path to increasing agni.

27. Devtas associated with skin ailments/"infection" (khaj, phoda, etc.). Per this teaching, various commonly worshipped, less "famous" folk deities (referenced generally , e.g., local Bhomiya ji, Ramdev ji-type deities) specialize precisely in this Jal Tatva/anumahanu-based infection science — meaning going to such a deity for a skin ailment, minor of fering in hand, is described as a genuinely effective, tar geted remedy , since these deities hold particular mastery over the anu/mahanu mechanism controlling the body's water element.

28. The three elements needed to consciously work with one's own chakras/water tatva, and the specific tool for each. Per this teaching: Agni (fire) is needed to carry jal tatva upward — cultivated via havan . Vayu (air) is needed to give the rising jal tatva its shape/form — cultivated via mantra jaap . Jal (water) itself needs no separate cultivation — the practitioner's own body , already ~70% water, already supplies it.

29. Chakras ar e, in principle, unlimited/uncountable. Per this teaching, because a chakra is fundamentally just a "shape" of water given form by air and lifted by fire, there is in principle no fixed, countable limit to chakras — new chakra-forms can and do keep forming further and further up (or wherever agni carries the jal tatva), forming an ongoing, potentially unlimited chain/sequence rather than a fixed set of seven.

30. Cr ossing a chakra means cr ossing a "unit" of vayu, not a fixed physical structur e. Per this teaching, when practitioners speak of "crossing" a particular chakra, they are, in this teaching's framework, actually crossing a specific unit/portion of vayu (air) that has taken shape as that chakra — and since these units are ef fectively unlimited, this crossing process itself is unlimited/uncountable rather than bounded to exactly seven distinct chakras.

31. Negative energy can travel along with vayu, entering chakras. Per this teaching, since chakras are shaped by vayu (air), and vayu is a medium negativity can travel through, negative ener gy absolutely can enter along with the very same air -based mechanism that shapes chakras — referenced as covered in more depth in a separate, dedicated 40-minute Ashaeiynn session on "V ayu Tatva" specifically .

32. Chakras can be "eaten"/consumed by tantrik practitioners — explained mechanically , not literally . Per this teaching, when a tantrik claims to have "eaten" or removed someone's chakras, this refers to interfering with the specific vayu-shaped "location" where jal tatva would otherwise take its form and receive incoming ener gy — chakras themselves, as an ongoing chain phenomenon, cannot truly be permanently taken away or made non-regenerable, since the underlying water/air/fire mechanism that produces them continues functioning as long as the practitioner lives, drinks water , and breathes.

33. Grahas (planetary influences) act thr ough a separate mechanism fr om chakras. Per this teaching, grahas do not operate "through" or by directly consuming chakras — they act through their own distinct mechanism. Example given: a weak Mangal (Mars) placement is associated with symptoms like abdominal pain, increased anger , physical injuries (especially to the head), and bloodrelated issues — with the specific bodily region af fected corresponding to a lower set of chakras.

34. Why an aura-checker might r eport "lower chakras tr oubled, upper chakras fine" for a Mars-r elated issue. Per this teaching, if only the lower body region is symptomatic while everything above functions normally , this indicates the person's jal tatva itself is not deficient (since the same water successfully rises through and functions well in the upper chakras) — the actual deficiency lies specifically in vayu (air), meaning the practical remedy is to strengthen one's vayu tatva, achieved most directly through mantra jaap (and supportively via practices like ajapa jaap, kapalbhati, and anulom-vilom).

35. Differ ent mantras ar e associated with differ ent colors and specific effects on chakras (bija mantras). Per this teaching, each individual mantra has its own associated color and its own specific jaap-based ef fect; bija (seed) mantras in particular are described as shaping specific chakra-related ener gy patterns, distinct from generic Reiki-style ener gy work — this is stated to make a genuine dif ference compared to generic healing techniques.

36. What "mantra dut" (mantra messengers) specifically do for this water -element mechanism. Per this teaching, a mantra dut's specific job is to ensure that the jal tatva stabilized at a given chakra keeps moving upward properly and does not get stuck at any one point; mantra dut are described as extremely versatile — capable, per this teaching, of essentially anything, including forming an entirely new chakra at a location where none previously existed, carrying jal tatva upward on the practitioner's behalf.

37. Advanced practitioners exist within Ashaeiynn whose specific experiences and identities ar e deliberately kept private. Per this teaching, out of roughly 250 people present in the community , many are functioning at an advanced level, but their names and specific practices are never publicly disclosed — naming them is described as risking disruption ("bhang") to their ongoing sadhna. A
specific, current example (kept anonymous) is described: a student able to see through multiple walls/buildings, and to see internal body structures (veins, bones) directly .

38. Why Ashaeiynn deliberately limits how much it publicly demonstrates or discloses. Per this teaching, the community's purpose is not to showcase powers as proof, but to connect people to Gurudev and to Ram-bhakti itself — anything not genuinely rooted in that devotion is described as ultimately of no real use ("jo Ram ka nahi, wo hamare kisi kaam ka nahi"), even though Ashaeiynn is explicitly described as a "third eye activation center ."

39. Why young/newer practitioners with str ong emerging abilities ar e specifically pr otected fr om public exposur e. Per this teaching, describing children/newer practitioners who can already perceive distant events or others' physical ailments: publicizing such abilities invites hostile "counter -attack" from skeptical outsiders, and such young practitioners — still emotionally "raw" — can develop self-doubt when challenged, which can cause the supporting shakti to withdraw; the described intent behind this protection is to prevent a world eager to instill doubt in others from damaging a genuine, still-developing gift.

40. A caution about certain public spiritual figur es who pr oduce "written pr oof"/pr edictions for show . Per this teaching, some public spiritual figures are described as producing written slips/predictions ("parcha") as a form of public demonstration — referenced without naming individuals, at Bhaiya's explicit request, as a contrast to Ashaeiynn's own approach of not seeking public validation through such demonstrations.

41. Element-specific sadhna is possible and is actively practiced within the community . Per this teaching, focused sadhna on a single specific element (e.g., specifically on Agni Tatva) is both possible and already being practiced — one specific, anonymized practitioner is referenced as having been engaged in dedicated Agni Tatva sadhna for roughly two years at the time of this session.

42. The overall closing intent of this session's teaching. Per this teaching, the purpose of walking through the jaltatva/chakra/infection mechanism in this much mechanical detail is so that practitioners understand these are not fixed, mystical absolutes but functioning systems governed by agni, vayu, and jal working together — and that as personal experience (via jaap and drishti) deepens over time, the underlying reality of these subtle mechanisms becomes increasingly apparent to the practitioner directly , rather than remaining abstract teaching.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Time/fate is powerful even over God (illustrated via Ram waiting through Sawan month despite already knowing Sita's location) — destiny cannot be broken except through the guru's will, and adverse periods should be met with self-protective caution ("bachav"), not aggressive action. New members should watch the "Mool Tatva" video and aim for a minimum of 15–20 lakh jaap repetitions as a starting benchmark. Manifestation power grows with sustained practice (3+ years), but desiring something outside one's own destiny/grahas invites universal backlash — keep ener gy reserves strong to absorb this. Drishti is a "necessary evil": necessary because it prevents confusion/wandering, "evil" because it demands constant heightened vigilance and comes with real responsibility . All chakras are fundamentally made of the same Jal Tatva (water element) — dif fering only in color , not in underlying substance; chakras are shaped by vayu (air) and lifted/relocated by agni (fire), and can shift position ("displacement") rather than staying permanently fixed. "Kundalini reaching sahasrar" mechanically means jal-tatva chakra ener gy has been carried, via suf ficient agni, all the way up to the crown position. External shaktipat/kundalini pushes beyond a practitioner's own agni capacity can leave a "gap" of inaccessible ener gy , increasing vulnerability to negativity even when standard aura checks show nothing wrong.

A saint's genuine "positive push" reserves higher -Dimension shakti for a devotee in advance, but it only becomes usable once the devotee's own agni becomes strong enough to reach it — explaining why some genuine saints are unfairly called "frauds" when a devotee's own ef fort falls short. Three ways to increase agni: mantra jaap (steady), tapasya/vrat (fasting/austerity), and havan (fastest and most powerful). The three-part working formula: agni via havan, vayu via mantra jaap, jal needs no separate cultivation (~70% of the body already). Chakras are, in principle, unlimited/uncountable — not fixed at exactly seven — since each is just a shaped "unit" of vayu carrying jal tatva. Advanced practitioners' identities and specific experiences (including documented abilities like seeing through walls or viewing internal body structures) are deliberately kept private to protect their ongoing sadhna and shield newer/younger practitioners from public skepticism. This session included genuine live sangat interaction (a lar ge rapid-fire Q&A round with multiple named and unnamed participants), so Part III (Curated Conversational Q&A) is included for this session. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 63, English)
Time, Destiny , and the Science of Jal Tatva
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live satsang session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siyaram."

Q1. Why did Bhagwan Ram wait an entir e month befor e acting on Sita's location, even though he alr eady knew wher e she was? A: Per this teaching, this illustrates that time ("samay") is powerful even over God — Ram waited through the entire Sawan (monsoon) month without telling anyone, and even his close friend Sugriv for got his promise to help during this period under the influence of maya, which cannot be countered until the appointed time arrives.

Q2. Did Hanuman Ji Maharaj also forget to help during this period, despite his devotion? A: Yes — per this teaching, despite being described as foremost among the wise and constantly absorbed in remembering Ram, Hanuman Ji Maharaj himself remained unaware of the need to help Sugriv for the entire Sawan month, illustrating that "samay bada balwan" (time is exceedingly powerful) applies even to the greatest devotees.

Q3. Can a person br eak or change their own destiny thr ough personal willpower? A: No — per this teaching, destiny cannot be broken by a person's own will; it can only change if and when the practitioner's own guru wills it.

Q4. What should someone do during a difficult or adverse period in life? A: Per this teaching, the person should focus purely on self-protection ("bachav") rather than aggressive, front-foot action, and should seek their guru's help and guidance during such times.

Q5. What should a first-time attendee do to begin practicing with Ashaeiynn? A: Per this teaching, first-time attendees should watch the "Mool Tatva" video and begin their own jaap alongside it, aiming for a minimum of 15–20 lakh repetitions as a starting benchmark, after which focused shaktis can be sent to support that practitioner .

Q6. What is the long-term effect of thr ee-plus years of sustained jaap/drishti practice? A: Per this teaching, the practitioner develops an accompanying unseen power that supports them at every step, guiding right from wrong, showing the path forward, and revealing "the other world" alongside the ordinary one — along with genuine manifestation power , meaning sincere wishes are described as certain to eventually occur .

Q7. If something I want conflicts with my own astr ological influences (grahas), will I still get it? A: Per this teaching, yes, eventually — but it will be delayed until that specific graha's influencing period naturally passes, unless the practitioner's own mantra shakti is strong enough to actively resolve the obstruction with directed ener gy , in which case it can happen much faster .

Q8. What happens if someone manifests something that was never actually meant to be theirs? A: Per this teaching, "the whole universe" turns against them, because what was gained was ef fectively taken from whoever it was truly destined for , and that displaced effect inevitably seeks some form of retribution — practitioners are advised to keep strong ener gy reserves specifically to absorb and rebound from this kind of backlash.

Q9. Why is drishti (subtle sight) described as a "necessary evil"? A: Per this teaching, it's "necessary" because without it a person remains confused and wanders between dif ferent babas, pandits, and pirs/fakirs seeking answers; it's "evil" because it makes a person
far more consciously alert and vigilant than before, which is itself a real burden/responsibility .

Q10. Does a genuinely advanced third-eye practitioner take personal cr edit for good outcomes? A: No — per this teaching, a practitioner with two-plus years of experience never claims "it happened because of me"; they recognize outcomes as what "Ram rach rakha" (already ordained by Ram) while still continuing sincere ef fort themselves.

Q1 1. What is this session's cor e teaching about, and what two numbers define it? A: Per this teaching, it's about the science of Jal Tatva (water element) and infection, built on 1 1 anu (particles) and 21 mahanu (great-particles).

Q12. What is a "Dwait Sangam," per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, it is a significant confluence point between the 1 1 anu and 21 mahanu, connected to four distinct subtle lokas (layers) existing in the space between the earth's surface and the sky — not the conventional earth/sky/netherworld triad.

Q13. Are all chakras made of differ ent elements (fire, water , air , earth), as commonly believed? A: No — per this teaching, contrary to common belief, all chakras are fundamentally made of the same Jal Tatva (water element); only their outward colors dif fer, not their underlying substance.

Q14. How do chakras actually form, mechanically , per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, chakras are tiny droplet-like clusters of water-element molecules arranged into distinct structures at each chakra location; when ener gy strikes these clusters, they rotate and emit their characteristic color as a "beam."

Q15. Why is r oughly 70% of the human body water , in relation to chakras, per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, because the chakras themselves are fundamentally water -based, this connects directly to the commonly cited fact that the body is approximately 70% water .

Q16. When fire (agni) incr eases in the body , does the water element (jal tatva) get consumed or reduced? A: No — per this teaching, agni does not consume or reduce jal tatva; it transforms and relocates it (like evaporation into steam), carrying it from a lower position to a higher one while it remains fundamentally water -based throughout.

Q17. Do chakras stay permanently fixed in one location? A: No — per this teaching, chakras can shift position ("displacement") — a chakra can leave its usual location and reform at a new position once rising jal-tatva ener gy (carried by agni) reaches a suitable spot and condenses there.

Q18. What does it actually mean, mechanically , when someone says their kundalini shakti has "r eached the sahasrar" (cr own chakra)? A: Per this teaching, it means the practitioner's jal-tatva-based chakra ener gy , normally at a lower position, has been carried by suf ficiently intense agni all the way up to the crown position — shaped along the way by vayu (air).

Q19. Can r eceiving a powerful shaktipat/kundalini-awakening fr om someone else ever backfir e? A: Yes — per this teaching, if someone else's power pushes a practitioner's chakra ener gy far higher than the practitioner's own agni (personal fire/tapasya capacity) can sustain, a "gap" forms, leaving the practitioner unable to access their own prayer/mantra shakti at that new position, and thus more vulnerable to negativity , even if standard aura checks show nothing wrong.

Q20. What is a genuine "positive push" fr om a saint, and why doesn't it always seem to work? A: Per this teaching, a genuine positive push lifts a devotee's chakra ener gy to a far higher Dimension and reserves that shakti for them in advance — but it only becomes usable once the devotee's own agni becomes strong enough to reach it; without that personal ef fort, the reserved blessing remains present but inaccessible, which is why some devotees see no visible results despite a genuine blessing.

Q21. Why do some genuine saints get unfairly called "frauds"? A: Per this teaching, when a devotee's own agni never becomes strong enough to reach the elevated Dimension a saint's blessing reserved for them, promised results simply don't materialize for that person, leading outside observers to wrongly blame the saint — when the actual shortfall is in the recipient's own undeveloped personal effort/agni.

Q22. What ar e the three main ways to incr ease one's own agni (fir e/inner energy)? A: Per this teaching, they are: mantra jaap (steady increase), tapasya/vrat — austerity/fasting (letting internal "tap" build by reducing external intake), and havan, described as the fastest and most powerful method.

Q23. What did Lord Shiva teach about the r elative power of tapasya versus havan? A: Per this teaching, per Lord Shiva's own stated wisdom, the fruit of a thousand havans exists within a single mantra jaap performed by a true tapasvi practicing sustained, unbroken tapasya and brahmacharya — but absent that level of personal discipline, havan remains the most accessible, reliable path.

Q24. Are there specific deities associated with skin ailments like "khaj" or "phoda" (infections)? A: Per this teaching, yes — various folk deities specialize precisely in this Jal Tatva/anu-mahanu-based infection science, holding particular mastery over the mechanism controlling the body's water element, making them a genuinely ef fective, tar geted remedy for such ailments.

Q25. What is the thr ee-part practical formula for working with one's own chakras/water element? A: Per this teaching: agni (fire, to carry jal tatva upward) is cultivated via havan; vayu (air , to shape the rising jal tatva) is cultivated via mantra jaap; jal (water) itself needs no separate cultivation, since the practitioner's own body is already roughly 70% water .

Q26. Are there really only seven chakras, as commonly taught? A: No — per this teaching, chakras are, in principle, unlimited/uncountable, since each is fundamentally just a "shape" of water given form by air and lifted by fire; new chakra-forms can keep forming as agni continues carrying jal tatva further upward.

Q27. Can negative energy travel into a person's chakras along with vayu (air)? A: Yes — per this teaching, since chakras are shaped by vayu, and vayu is a medium negativity can travel through, negative ener gy can absolutely enter along with the same air - based mechanism that shapes chakras (this is covered in more depth in a separate, dedicated Ashaeiynn session on Vayu Tatva).

Q28. What does it actually mean when a tantrik claims to have "eaten" or removed someone's chakras? A: Per this teaching, this refers to interfering with the specific vayu-shaped "location" where jal tatva would otherwise take form — chakras themselves cannot truly be permanently taken away or made non-regenerable, since the underlying water/air/fire mechanism keeps functioning as long as the practitioner lives, drinks water , and breathes.

Q29. Do planetary influences (grahas) act by dir ectly consuming or damaging chakras?
